purpose: Research matrix of indoor navigation/positioning technologies to find the fastest CREDIBLE path for Mall@Reds. Research targets only. CRITICAL: every capability/pricing/support field is a research QUESTION, not an asserted fact — requires_live_verification=true throughout. Do not treat model memory as final truth.

current_state_from_audit.route_graph: mall_nodes / mall_edges in Postgres (migration 005); real Dijkstra pathfinding (routingService.ts + build-route edge fn).
current_state_from_audit.positioning_today: NONE indoor. GPS used only for nearest-mall selection. On-map 'GPS'/'Tracking' UI is decorative (overstates capability).
current_state_from_audit.platform: Vite/React PWA (web-first). Any solution must weigh web/PWA support heavily.
current_state_from_audit.integration_point: A positioning source must resolve the shopper to (or near) a mall_nodes node so the existing Dijkstra route can re-origin from real position instead of the default entrance.

preliminary_reasoning_pending_verificati.fastest_credible_web_first_path: QR anchors + smartphone dead-reckoning. Rationale: works in the existing React PWA on any phone, needs ZERO mall-installed hardware (just printed QR at known nodes), and plugs straight into the existing mall_nodes graph — a QR payload IS a node_id, which fixes the audit's 'current_anchor_node_id never written' defect and replaces the manual 'Done' taps with real movement. Honest, cheap, shippable.
preliminary_reasoning_pending_verificati.map_rendering_upgrade_optional: Mapbox indoor or MapsIndoors could replace the schematic SVG later, but rendering is NOT the blocker — positioning is.
preliminary_reasoning_pending_verificati.hardware_heavy_paths_deprioritized: BLE/Wi-Fi RTT/UWB need mall cooperation + capex and mostly fail the web-PWA constraint; revisit only if a partner mall funds infrastructure.

summary.recommended_proof: QR-anchor scan-to-locate on one Mall@Reds floor, re-origining the existing Dijkstra route; measure whether shoppers reach the correct store.
